mohan: FYI hitting a strange perf cliff when the kernel selector chooses the YARN variant for RoPE NTK-scaled meshes on mixtral-7b longctx runs. Repro attached below, small profiling paste.

eva: ugh, can you paste the exact selector config and batch sizes? Is this deterministic or flakey? :eyes:

mohan: deterministic on our test harness (longctx=64k, synthetic tokens). selector config is below. noticed latency jumps ~3x and perplexity spike on some prompts.

mohan: ```json
{"model": "mixtral-7b", "rope_variant": "ntk->yarn", "kernel_selector": "auto", "batching": {"max_tokens": 4096, "max_batch": 16, "prefill_parallelism": 2}, "kv_policy": "active_eviction=LRU,window=16384"}
```

sam: is this observed on mistral/llama too or only mixtral? any kernel crash logs? did selector fallback to a different kernel or fail open to CPU path?

mohan: mainly mixtral and qwen-7b experimental builds. llama-2-7b is fine. no kernel OOMs in dmesg, but we see lots of tiny kernel switches and head_kv rebinds in the runtime trace. snippet:

```
[pprof] mixtral-7b: kernel_switches=3142, avg_switch_ms=0.67, kv_rebinds=211, evictions/sec=9.8
[latency] p50=42ms => p50=130ms after selector=YARN pick
[ppl] baseline=17.9 => observed=23.4 on repro prompt set
```

kevin: that smells like thrashing between YARN optimized kernels (low mem) and the throughput kernels. The runtime's kernel selector heuristics consider seq_len dist + kv footprint; with NTK RoPE scaling the effective kernel memory estimate is wrong -> it picks YARN then we end up re-allocating big KV windows on the hot path. Can you repro with `kernel_selector: prefer_throughput`?

mohan: ran prefer_throughput. latency dropped back but CPU/GPU utilization changed. quick compare:

```
auto selector (YARN chosen): p50=128ms, p95=420ms, tokens/s=510
prefer_throughput: p50=46ms, p95=120ms, tokens/s=1680
```

perf-bot: [metric-post] run=2039876555, job=mixtral-longctx-sweep, tag=rope-ntk-yarn, latency_p50=128, p95=420, tokens_per_sec=510, link=https://ci/reports/2039876555

eva: ok that strongly points at kernel routing. We probably need a small adjustment: when rope scaling factor > 1.0 AND head_kv_dim >= 128, bias the selector away from YARN. Also adjust batching heuristic to reduce small-batch prefill that causes repeated rebinds. Proposed quick diff:

```
if rope_scale > 1.0 && head_kv_dim >= 128:
    selector.bias += SKIP_YARN
batching.prefill_threshold_tokens = max(512, batching.max_tokens / 8)
```

sam: any perf regression on memory-limited dedicated nodes if we bias away from YARN? we might increase per-request mem footprint.

kevin: yes we trade memory for stability. but for longctx workloads it's acceptable; better than 3x latency spikes. We can make it a canary rollout to dedicated only first.

ops-bot: FYI created canary rollout config `canary/rope-selector-safety` targeting dedicated pool `dedicated-gpu-pool-a`, 10% traffic, rollout window 2h. CI checks: smoke perf, kv-eviction-rate, OOM alerts.

mohan: running a focused sweep now across models (mixtral,mistral,qwen,llama). I'll post results here. Early note: qwen-7b shows smaller cliff but same pattern; mistral-7b less affected. Llama unaffected.

perf-bot: [metric-post] run=2039876660, tag=canary/rope-selector-safety, mixtral_p50=52, p95=140, kv_evictions=1.2/sec

mohan: initial canary results look promising. I'm opening a PR to add the selector bias + batching prefill change and a small eval gating job for perplexity regression on the repro prompt set.

eva: thanks. add a note in the PR to include model-specific safe ranges (rope_scale thresholds) per model. we should not hardcode one-size-fits-all.

kevin: I'll add a unit test for kernel_switch_count <= 50 on synthetic longctx to prevent regressions.

mohan: PR opened: https://git/repo/pulls/4521 -> will follow up with full sweep artifacts. :thumbsup:

sam: nice triage, team. once merged let's run a 24h soak on prod traffic sim config.

mohan: will do. closing loop after soak. :white_check_mark:
